definition: The Mark I Perceptron was a pioneering supervised image classification learning system developed by Frank Rosenblatt in 1958.
details: It was the first implementation of an artificial intelligence (AI) machine. It differs from the Perceptron which is a software architecture proposed in 1943 by Warren McCulloch and Walter Pitts, which was also employed in Mark I, and enhancements of which have continued to be an integral part of cutting edge AI technologies like the transformer.

explainer.lead: The Mark I Perceptron was a pioneering supervised image classification learning system built by Frank Rosenblatt in 1958. It matters as the first implementation of an artificial intelligence machine.

tiers.eli5: It was an early machine that learned to recognise pictures by being shown examples, built long before modern computers.
tiers.practitioner: No modern engineering workflow uses the Mark I itself; it is studied as the historical first hardware implementation of a learning machine. A pitfall is conflating it with the earlier Perceptron software architecture of 1943.
tiers.paperLevel: It is the first hardware implementation of an AI machine, distinct from the 1943 McCulloch–Pitts Perceptron software architecture, which it also employed. No formula is attached to the device itself.

explainer.example: Rosenblatt's 1958 system learned to classify images under supervision, using the McCulloch–Pitts Perceptron architecture inside a physical machine.
